successCriteria.description: The service interface exposes exactly four methods — getPolicyForLeaveType, getActivePolicies, calculateEntitlement, and validatePolicy — with the signatures specified in PLAN.md Phase 8 (getPolicyForLeaveType returns Promise<LeavePolicy>, getActivePolicies returns Promise<LeavePolicy[]>, calculateEntitlement returns number, validatePolicy returns boolean).
calculateEntitlement returns full entitlementDays when hireDate is on or before Jan 1 of the fiscalYear (e.g. hire July 2024, fiscalYear 2025 → 20; hire Jan 1 2025, fiscalYear 2025 → 20).

calculateEntitlement pro-rates mid-year hires by whole months remaining (11 - hireMonth), floored: hire Jan 15 → 11 months → floor(20*11/12)=18; hire Feb 1 → 10 months → 16; hire Jun 15 → 6 months → 10; hire Nov 30 → 1 month → 1; hire Dec 1 → 0 months → 0.

calculateEntitlement applies maxAccumulation as a cap after pro-ration when maxAccumulation is defined (entitlement 30, cap 25, pre-fiscal-year hire → 25; entitlement 60, cap 40, Jan 15 hire → 40), and does not cap when maxAccumulation is undefined or when the result is already below the cap.
calculateEntitlement always returns a non-negative integer (never a fraction, never negative).

getPolicyForLeaveType resolves the leave type by code, rejects with NOT_FOUND when the type does not exist, rejects with POLICY_VIOLATION when the type is inactive, and rejects with POLICY_VIOLATION when zero or multiple active policies exist for that type; returns the single active policy otherwise.

getActivePolicies fetches all policies and returns only those with isActive === true; returns an empty array when no policies exist or all are inactive; propagates repository errors without swallowing them.

validatePolicy returns true for a structurally valid policy (non-empty policyName/leaveTypeId, positive integer entitlementDays, non-negative optional accrualRate/maxAccumulation/minimumNoticeDays, boolean requiresManagerApproval and isActive) and false for any violation including null/undefined/non-object input, empty/whitespace strings, zero/negative/non-integer entitlementDays, negative optional numerics, and non-boolean flags.
The leave-policy barrel (index.ts) re-exports ILeavePolicyService and LeavePolicyService (and AppError) so downstream modules import the service only through the module's public entry point.

Jest unit tests exist under tests/unit/modules/leave-policy/ covering the pro-ration edge cases (Jan 15 → 18, Dec 1 → 0, pre-fiscal-year → full), maxAccumulation capping, validatePolicy accept/reject paths, and getPolicyForLeaveType/getActivePolicies behavior including error cases — and all tests pass.

constraints: The service must inject ILeavePolicyRepository and ILeaveTypeRepository (from Phase 2 and Phase 3) — no direct database access inside the service (GP-001).
All cross-module imports must go through the leave-policy module's public barrel (index.ts), never from internal files directly (ARCHITECTURE.md dependency rule).
Strict TypeScript must pass with no implicit any and strict null checks; the optional fields (accrualRate, maxAccumulation, minimumNoticeDays) must be checked for undefined/null before use.

Domain errors must use the AppError class carrying a code string matching the error response contract (NOT_FOUND for missing leave type, POLICY_VIOLATION for inactive type / zero or multiple active policies) — no raw Error throws for domain failures.
No unhandled promise rejections (GP-006): async methods must either resolve with a value or reject with a typed AppError; repository errors must propagate, not be swallowed.
outOfScope: LeaveBalanceService and balance initialization (Phase 9) — this phase only provides calculateEntitlement as a pure function; it does not create balance records.
LeaveRequestService, routes, overlap detection, and the full leave lifecycle (Phase 10).
HTTP routes/controllers for leave-policy — this phase is service-layer only; no Fastify route definitions.
Audit record creation for policy reads — getPolicyForLeaveType and getActivePolicies are read-only operations and do not require audit records (GP-002 applies to state-changing operations only).
Accrual scheduling, carryover rules, and year-end rollover jobs — the binding rule specifies annual lump-sum allocation; ongoing accrual mechanics are not part of this service.

entityInvariants.invariant: A leave type may have at most one active policy at any time; getPolicyForLeaveType enforces this by rejecting with POLICY_VIOLATION when zero or multiple active policies are found for a given leave type.
The calculated entitlement is always a non-negative integer bounded above by maxAccumulation when that field is defined; pro-ration never produces a fractional or negative result.
Only active leave types may be used for policy resolution; an inactive leave type causes getPolicyForLeaveType to reject with POLICY_VIOLATION regardless of whether policies exist.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Rejects with AppError code NOT_FOUND when the leave type code does not resolve to a row; rejects with AppError code POLICY_VIOLATION when the leave type is inactive or when zero or multiple active policies exist for that type. Returns the single active LeavePolicy on success.

Resolves with an array of LeavePolicy objects filtered to isActive === true (possibly empty); propagates repository-level errors without transformation. Never rejects for "no results" — an empty array is a valid response.

Pure synchronous function — never throws under normal input; returns a non-negative integer. Fiscal year start is Jan 1 of fiscalYear. Hires on or before that date receive full entitlementDays; later hires are pro-rated by (11 - hireMonth) whole months, floored, then capped at maxAccumulation if defined.

Pure synchronous function — never throws; returns false for null/undefined/non-object input or any structural violation rather than throwing. Returns true only when all required and optional fields satisfy their type and range constraints.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The service must operate on the LeavePolicy interface as defined in leave-policy.model.ts — entitlementDays (number), maxAccumulation (number | undefined), accrualRate (number | undefined), minimumNoticeDays (number | undefined), requiresManagerApproval (boolean), isActive (boolean). The pro-ration and validation logic must reference these exact field names.

The service must call ILeavePolicyRepository.findAll() for getActivePolicies and ILeavePolicyRepository.findActiveByLeaveTypeId(leaveTypeId) for getPolicyForLeaveType — matching the repository interface method names and signatures declared in Phase 3.

The service must call ILeaveTypeRepository.findByCode(code) to resolve a leave type by its LeaveTypeCode — matching the repository interface method declared in Phase 2. The returned LeaveType.isActive field drives the active-type check.

The pro-ration algorithm must match the BINDING business rule in reconciled.json: annual lump-sum allocation at fiscal year start (Jan 1); mid-year hires pro-rated by whole months remaining (11 - hireMonth), rounded down; maxAccumulation caps the result. The fiscal year boundary is calendar year (Jan 1 – Dec 31), organisation-wide.

The error codes used by the service (NOT_FOUND, POLICY_VIOLATION) must match the Error Response Contract section of ARCHITECTURE.md: not found → 404 (NOT_FOUND), policy violation → 400 (POLICY_VIOLATION).

integrationPoints.why: LeaveBalanceService.initializeBalancesForEmployee will call LeavePolicyService.getActivePolicies and calculateEntitlement to compute per-policy entitlements when creating balance records for a new employee.

LeaveRequestService will call getPolicyForLeaveType to resolve the policy governing a leave type (for notice-period checks, approval-flag checks, and entitlement validation) during request submission and approval.
The service interface and getPolicyForLeaveType parameter depend on the LeaveTypeCode enum from src/shared/types for type-safe leave type identification.
